headline: Flexion Robotics trains humanoids for complex office tasks autonomously
summary: Swiss startup Flexion Robotics uses reinforcement learning and simulation to train humanoid robots for complex office chores, enabling autonomous operation in unfamiliar settings.
details: Flexion Robotics, a Swiss startup founded by ex-Nvidia researchers, has developed a method to train humanoid robots for complex tasks. This includes skills like opening doors, climbing stairs, and carrying boxes.
The core of their approach involves teaching individual skills in simulation. A master AI algorithm then determines how to combine these learned skills to execute complex instructions.

Unlike most demo humanoids trained via teleoperation for specific, repetitive tasks, Flexion's system trains robots autonomously in simulation with limited human instruction. This makes their robots more efficient and reliable when encountering unfamiliar environments.

A demonstration video showcased a modified Unitree humanoid robot autonomously fulfilling a multi-step command: "A parcel with snacks has been delivered for Flexion. Retrieve it using the stairs and come up using the elevator. Then unpack it and place the items into the empty drawer on the shelf in the snack area."

The main AI model learns by processing videos of humans performing various actions. It then matches these observations with skills acquired in simulation to perform tasks in the real world, controlling the robot's movements and balance.

Nikita Rudin, Flexion's cofounder and CEO, identifies extensive reinforcement learning as the "secret ingredient." This method trains computers to master tasks through trial and error, applied across all layers of the software.

Industry analysts, like George Chowdhury of ABI Research, emphasize that the AI models powering humanoids are the truly revolutionary aspect. ABI Research forecasts the market for robot foundation models could reach $150 billion by 2036.
Flexion Robotics is actively collaborating with various robotics companies and ensures its software is compatible across different humanoid platforms, potentially increasing its commercial value.

headline_marked: [[JetBrains Junie AI coding agent leaves Beta]], secures #1 spot on SWE-Rebench benchmark
headline: JetBrains Junie AI coding agent leaves Beta, secures #1 spot on SWE-Rebench benchmark
summary: JetBrains' official AI coding agent, Junie, is now generally available after topping the SWE-Rebench coding agent benchmark. It features a 'plan before coding' mode, native IDE debugger integration, and flexible model strategy.
details: JetBrains' official AI coding agent, Junie, has officially left its Beta phase and is now generally available. It recently secured the number-one spot on the authoritative SWE-Rebench coding agent benchmark, achieving 61.6% resolved and a 72.7% pass@5.

Junie aims to solve the problem of AI assistants writing code in the wrong direction, leading to wasted time. Its heavyweight upgrades include a 'plan before coding' mode, direct native IDE debugger integration, and comprehensive code reviews with complete project context.

The 'plan before coding' mode creates a structured document outlining product requirements, technical design, and delivery stages before any code is written. Developers can review and approve this plan directly in their editor, significantly reducing invalid executions and token waste.

Unlike most coding agents that add log statements, Junie can drive your IDE's debugger. It can start or join a debug session, launch run configurations, debug tests, and set breakpoints anywhere needed.

Junie also supports a flexible, vendor-lock-in-free model strategy. This empowers developers to utilize either frontier models for powerful reasoning or local runtimes for cost efficiency, allowing control over task costs.

The agent asks targeted questions when requirements are ambiguous, preventing guesswork. This approach ensures the agent doesn't wander, keeping bills low and making delegation affordable for frequent use.
